summary: Introductory discovery between Redwood AE/SE and OrionBridge partnerships/engineering. Discussed potential go-to-market integration (marketplace listing and co-sell), technical integration options (hosted API, dedicated pools, private/VPC deployments), and operational requirements (KMS, SOC2, SSO). Agreed to a technical deep-dive and to exchange security and topology docs; next step is pilot scoping and pricing.
transcript:
00:00 Liam O'Connell: Hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Liam from Redwood, i'm the AE on this motion. we got Priya our SE and Diego on the call. Alex? thanks for taking time.
00:08 Alex Martinez: yeah thanks Liam, excited to learn more — we think there's a good fit between OrionBridge's marketplace and Redwood's inference offering, especially for enterprise customers who want managed inference.
00:18 Priya Rao: quick intro from my side, i focus on infra and deployment patterns — we've worked a lot on Dedicated + Private flows for partners.
00:26 Sofia Anders: great, i'm Sofia CTO, i'll be focused on technical integration. ravi is our cloud lead who manages gpu fleet.
00:33 Ravi Patel: hey all, yeah hi. quick note, OrionBridge primarily resells cloud + infra and we also operate an edge GPU fabric for some customers.
00:42 Liam: perfect. high level, how do you see us working together? marketplace listing, co-sell, maybe managed private deployments for large ISVs?
00:50 Alex: marketplace listing is the primary avenue; second is tightly integrated managed offers where we can provision dedicated pools for our largest clients. they ask for vpc and strict data residency often.
01:03 Priya: great — on Redwood side we have three common models: hosted API for easy self-serve, Redwood Dedicated (reserved gpu pools) for predictable throughput, and Redwood Private for VPC/on-prem installs. for managed partners we often do Dedicated or Private.
01:16 Sofia: when you say Private, do you mean full on-prem or a vpc-peered control plane?
01:22 Priya: both. Private can be customer-managed network with our control plane optionally in their VPC, or a full on-prem package. we integrate with KMS/HSM for key mgmt.
01:30 Ravi: important for us: KMS + audit logs and SSO. client compliance teams need SOC2, iso27001, and SAML sso; also RBAC at team level.
01:41 Diego Morales: yep that's in our enterprise checklist, we can share our security package. we also expose per-route logs through Redwood Console and have token-level cost breakdowns.
01:50 Alex: sounds good. on the infra side, what GPUs do you optimize for? we have H100 and A100 nodes across partners.
01:58 Priya: we optimize kernels for both H100 and A100; sequence length and model architecture affect kernel selection. we also provide quantization profiles to save costs.
02:07 Sofia: do you do automatic model fallback? say if first choice model is out of capacity we need graceful degradation.
02:13 Priya: yes, smart routing supports fallback to compatible model variants and region routing, and we can set policies by latency or cost.
02:20 Ravi: latency SLOs — for some customers sub-100ms is required for short synchronous queries. how do you保証 latency with batching?
02:29 Priya: continuous batching with workload-aware policies — we can prioritize low latency traffic and use smaller batch sizes or dedicated pools to hit sub-100ms. there's always a tradeoff with unit cost.
02:38 Alex: commercial question — how do partners get paid? revenue split? referral fees?
02:42 Liam: we have flexible models — referral commissions for marketplace, co-sell splits for enterprise, and managed services arrangements. we'll share standard partner terms but can tailor for large accounts.
02:52 Marta Lopez: one nit, many customers ask for price transparency per token and per-embedding; do you expose that?
02:58 Diego: yes Redwood API shows per-token costs and console breakdowns; for Dedicated we do committed pricing with usage reporting.
03:05 Sofia: security docs please — SOC2, pen test, encryption-at-rest keys, key rotation policies.
03:12 Liam: Agreed. i'll send SOC2 and security pack.
03:15 Ravi: for pilot we want a small benchmark — 3 models, 10k concurrent requests over day, sample datasets. is that straightforward?
03:23 Priya: we can run a benchmark; typically we ask for sample prompt sets and sequence length distribution — also expected QPS and burst patterns. we advise on quantization and batching profiles for cost.
03:33 Alex: are there any known partner integrations (SI/SaaS) you already have that we can reference?
03:38 Liam: yes, we've done integrations with a few cloud marketplaces and SI partners — i'll share reference case studies.
03:43 Sofia: regarding networking, we need to understand egress flows and data residency — do you support regional pinning?
03:49 Priya: yes per-region deployment options, and routing policies can pin to region; for private installs it's entirely under the customer's network.
03:57 Ravi: about quotas — can we provision guaranteed GPU counts for Dedicated? our customers want guaranteed capacity during launches.
04:04 Priya: Dedicated supports reserved GPU pools and autoscaling policies with burst capacity; that is usually part of a commit plan.
04:12 Alex: any blockers from your side to listing on our marketplace?
04:16 Liam: not really, we usually need a tech integration checklist, legal/terms alignment, and a partner listing asset.
04:22 Marta: what about identity — can customers sign in via our SSO and then access Redwood-managed offerings?
04:28 Diego: we support SAML SSO and can federate identities; for deeper integration we can do SCIM or SSO provisioning.
04:35 Sofia: i'm also curious about observability — we need traces and per-request metadata for compliance.
04:39 Priya: Redwood Console surfaces per-route/model dashboards, tracing hooks, and error analysis. we can push events to customer systems via webhooks or SIEM integrations.
04:49 Ravi: one practical question — do you allow customers to bring their own model weights? some of our clients want to run proprietary models.
04:55 Priya: yes, we support BYO models in Private and Dedicated contexts with model onboarding and kernel selection; we also have guidance for quantization.
05:03 Alex: any concerns around data exfil? enterprise teams worry about KV cache and prefix caching storing sensitive data.
05:11 Diego: we have KV cache controls and can purge caches; data retention policies can be enforced and audited. for strict cases we recommend Private deployment.
05:20 Marta: good to know. ok next steps?
05:22 Liam: i'll send partner one-pager, security deck, pricing spreadsheet. Priya will set up the infra deep-dive to go over benchmarks and topology. Ravi will share their VPC diagram and expected numbers.
05:31 Sofia: sounds good, we'll aim to get docs over by friday.
05:34 Alex: thanks everyone, excited to keep this moving.
05:37 Priya: thanks all, look forward to the deep-dive.
05:40 Diego: bye!
05:42 End of recording.

Notes on transcript: occasional transcription errors (e.g., 'KV cache' sometimes transcribed as 'kay vee cache'), speaker labels simplified; there was some crosstalk around 02:30 when discussing latency tradeoffs.
